title: Entropy-Bounded Empiricism: Regime-Dependent Validity in Galaxy Rotation Curves
description: Complete documentation of the Entropy-Bounded Empiricism (EBE) framework applied to the SPARC175 galaxy rotation curves. The paper reports regime-dependent model validity with 100% EFC success in the FLOW regime (62/62) and strong nonparametric evidence (Mann-Whitney p < 0.0001, Cliff's δ = 0.371), while a CMB null test (p = 0.251) shows no regime structure, supporting the framework's specificity to non-equilibrium systems.

key_results.main_finding: EFC achieves 100% success in the FLOW regime (62/62) with strong regime-dependent structure (p < 0.0001, Cliff's δ = 0.371), while the CMB shows no such structure (p = 0.251).
parameters_tested: Kruskal-Wallis H test with Dunn post-hoc

sealed_predictions.statement: Applying the EBE regime-classification pipeline to CMB angular power spectra will show no significant regime structure (p > 0.05, |δ| ≈ 0).
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Future high-precision CMB datasets or alternative power spectra analyses yielding significant regime separation under the same pipeline.

kill_criteria: KC1: Pre-registered replication on an independent rotation-curve dataset using fixed thresholds (L1 = 0.337, L2 = 0.427; FLOW: L < 0.337) yields a FLOW EFC success rate ≤ 80% or no significant separation from non-FLOW (Mann–Whitney p ≥ 0.05 and |Cliff's δ| ≤ 0.15).

KC2: After controlling for measurement quality (e.g., N_points stratification or regression adjustment), the regime effect vanishes (p ≥ 0.10 and |δ| ≤ 0.15), indicating the L–quality correlation fully explains the result.

KC3: Robustness failure: Across a pre-specified set of reasonable, model-blind L definitions and small boundary perturbations, ≥ 80% of variants lose significance (p ≥ 0.05) and effect size shrinks to |δ| ≤ 0.15.
KC4: CMB contradiction: Applying the identical regime-classification pipeline to updated CMB angular power spectra finds significant regime structure (p ≤ 0.01 or |δ| ≥ 0.30).

KC5: Information leakage: Demonstration that L (or S) relies on post-fit or model-dependent information; when recomputed with a strictly model-blind definition, the regime effect is not significant (p ≥ 0.05).

KC6: Cross-survey failure: In two or more independent surveys (e.g., THINGS, LITTLE THINGS, SPARC extensions), pre-registered tests with fixed thresholds yield FLOW success rate < 60% (chi-squared < 3) and no significant regime separation (p ≥ 0.05).

KC7: Direct entropy proxy refutation: Independent determinations of low-entropy systems (S < 0.25) identify ≥ 10 galaxies where EFC fits fail strongly (median chi-squared ≥ 5), decoupling FLOW from success.

KC8: Corrected resampling diagnostics: Re-running permutation/bootstrap tests with verified code places the observed effect within the central 90% of the null (p ≥ 0.10), eliminating evidence for non-random regime structure.
KC9: High-quality subsample inconsistency: In the N_points ≥ 50 subsample, FLOW does not outperform other regimes (p ≥ 0.05), contradicting the reported strengthening of the effect with data quality.
abstract_short: EBE framework: 100% EFC success in FLOW regime (62/62 galaxies). Mann-Whitney p<0.0001, Cliff's δ=0.371. CMB null test passes (p=0.251).
